newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles refinery erupts in early morning blaze.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles refinery erupts in early morning blaze.

text.p: A fire erupted at a key Los Angeles refinery Friday morning, sending plumes of smoke over a local freeway and slowing traffic.

The fire broke out at 5:15 a.m. at the sprawling Mobil Corp refinery in the Los Angeles suburb of Torrance. Thirty-five firefighters brought it under control in less than two hours. There were no injuries.
Mobil spokewsoman Chris Lewis said the fire started at a gasoline-making unit but the rest of the refinery was continuing to operate. The cause of the fire was unknown.
According to a Los Angeles television station, witnesses reported three explosions at the time of the fire.
The refinery makes 15 percent of the gasoline sold in Southern California and produces about 1.5 billion gallons of gasoline a year.
Local fire officials said a hazardous material team was called in to inspect the site and decontamination procedures were underway.
